summary: Fine-tuning makes the most sense after prompt engineering and RAG have been exhausted — the canonical 2026 sequence is Prompt → RAG → Fine-tune → Distill, moving right only when the cheaper option provably hits a wall. Most production systems layer all three, with fine-tuning reserved for consistent behavioral adaptation at scale, domain-specific tone/format enforcement, or latency-critical inference where system prompts are too costly. Base models in 2026 (Qwen3, Llama 4, Gemma 3) are strong enough out-of-the-box that the threshold for needing fine-tuning is higher than ever.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when the model's behavior remains inconsistent at scale after prompt engineering and RAG have both been tried and proven insufficient.
Choose fine-tuning when you need the model to internalize a specific style, tone, schema, or domain vocabulary that cannot be reliably injected via context at inference time.
Choose fine-tuning when latency or cost constraints make long system prompts or retrieval pipelines impractical for production traffic.
Choose fine-tuning when you are doing RLHF, DPO, or preference alignment to shift model behavior in ways that retrieval cannot address.

tools.name: Hugging Face AutoTrain
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-compute on Hugging Face infrastructure; GPU hours billed by instance type (T4 to H100); Inference Endpoints priced separately by instance/hour
features: No-code web UI for fine-tuning with zero scripting required
Supports LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, and full fine-tuning
Integrated with Hugging Face Hub — largest model repository in existence
Inference Endpoints for one-click deployment post fine-tuning
Flexible GPU hardware selection from T4 to A100 to H100
Configurable autoscaling policies for deployment
Active open-source community and extensive documentation
tools.best_for: Research, experimentation, and teams wanting access to the broadest model selection with a no-code entry point; natural fit for open-source-first organizations

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Training: ~$0.008/1K tokens for GPT-4o mini; inference on fine-tuned models billed at premium per-token rates above base model pricing; varies by model tier
features: Fully managed, no infrastructure required
Supports supervised fine-tuning and preference fine-tuning (DPO-style)
Integrates directly with OpenAI playground and API ecosystem
Automatic hyperparameter selection with optional manual overrides
Training metrics and loss curves available in dashboard
Fine-tuned models hosted and served by OpenAI
Easiest path for teams already using OpenAI APIs in production
tools.best_for: Enterprises and product teams already on the OpenAI stack who need behavioral customization of GPT models without any MLOps overhead

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Open source (free); Unsloth Pro with additional features and support available — pricing on request
features: 2–5x faster training speeds compared to standard HuggingFace Transformers
40% less VRAM usage enabling larger models on consumer hardware
QLoRA support allowing 20B models on a single RTX 4090
Excellent Colab notebooks for beginner-friendly onboarding
Supports LoRA, QLoRA, and full fine-tuning
Actively maintained with rapid support for new model releases
Works as backend for LLaMA-Factory web UI
tools.best_for: Individual developers and researchers fine-tuning on consumer or single-GPU hardware who need maximum speed and VRAM efficiency

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source and free; compute costs depend on your own GPU infrastructure or cloud
features: Web UI (LLaMA Board) providing zero-code fine-tuning experience
Supports DPO, PPO, KTO, ORPO, and SFT natively
Both instruction fine-tuning and continued pre-training supported
Can use Unsloth as backend for speed/VRAM gains
Easiest starting point for beginners among CLI/local tools
Broad model compatibility across architectures
Active community with frequent updates
tools.best_for: Beginners and practitioners who want a feature-rich web UI and support for advanced alignment methods (DPO, PPO, ORPO) without writing training code

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source and free; compute costs on your own infrastructure or cloud
features: YAML-based configuration for highly reproducible training runs
Multi-GPU and multi-node training support out of the box
Supports LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, and DPO
Flash Attention 2 integration for memory efficiency
Curriculum learning and dataset mixing support
Deeply flexible for custom training loops and experimental setups
Strong adoption in research and advanced practitioner communities
tools.best_for: Advanced practitioners and researchers who need maximum flexibility, reproducibility, and multi-GPU scale with full control over training configuration

tools.name: Together AI Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Per-token training pricing; fine-tuned model inference at competitive per-token rates; credits available for new accounts — check together.ai for current rates
features: Fully managed fine-tuning with no infrastructure overhead
FlashAttention and kernel optimizations for faster inference on fine-tuned models
REST API-based job submission and monitoring
Competitive inference pricing post fine-tuning
Supports LoRA and full fine-tuning jobs
Strong performance for latency-sensitive production deployments
tools.best_for: Teams needing managed fine-tuning on open-weight models with optimized inference speed and lower latency than self-hosted alternatives

tools.name: Vertex AI (Google Cloud) Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Supervised fine-tuning billed per training hour on TPUs/GPUs; Gemini fine-tuning has separate per-token pricing; enterprise agreements available
features: Fully managed MLOps pipeline integrated with Google Cloud ecosystem
Supports supervised fine-tuning and RLHF for Gemini models
Model Garden provides access to open-source models alongside proprietary
Enterprise-grade security, compliance, and VPC support
Integrated with BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Vertex AI Pipelines
Evaluation and monitoring tooling built in
TPU access for high-throughput training workloads
tools.best_for: Enterprises already in the Google Cloud ecosystem who need fine-tuning of Gemini or open-source models with full MLOps, compliance, and data governance

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Per-token training cost varies by model; provisioned throughput required for fine-tuned model serving, billed by model unit/hour; check AWS pricing page
features: Fully managed fine-tuning within AWS infrastructure — no GPU provisioning
Continued pre-training and instruction fine-tuning supported
Deep integration with AWS security (IAM, VPC, PrivateLink)
Data stays within AWS environment for compliance-sensitive workloads
Provisioned throughput for low-latency fine-tuned model serving
Supports custom model import for fine-tuned weights
Native integration with S3 for training data and model artifacts
tools.best_for: AWS-native enterprises with strict data residency, compliance, or security requirements who need managed fine-tuning without leaving the AWS ecosystem

tools.name: Modal
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-second GPU compute; H100s, A100s, T4s available; ~$0.00139/GPU-second for A100; free tier includes monthly credits
supported_models: Any HuggingFace-compatible model including Llama 4, Qwen3, Mistral, Gemma 3, DeepSeek
features: Serverless GPU compute — spin up training jobs in seconds with Python decorators
No DevOps or Kubernetes knowledge required
Bring your own training script (Axolotl, TRL, Unsloth all work on Modal)
Pay only for exact GPU seconds consumed
Fast cold-start times compared to traditional cloud VM provisioning
Ideal for running periodic or event-driven fine-tuning pipelines
Free monthly compute credits make experimentation low-risk
tools.best_for: ML engineers who want cloud GPU access without infrastructure management, running their own training code (Axolotl, TRL, Unsloth) on demand

tools.name: TRL (Transformer Reinforcement Learning)
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source and free; compute on your own hardware or any cloud
supported_models: Any HuggingFace-compatible model — Llama 4, Qwen3, Gemma 3, Mistral, DeepSeek, Phi-4
features: Official HuggingFace library for SFT, DPO, PPO, RLHF, and KTO
SFTTrainer and DPOTrainer abstractions simplify alignment workflows
Tightly integrated with Transformers, PEFT, and Accelerate
Used as backend by Axolotl and other frameworks
Supports distributed training across multiple GPUs
Rapidly updated to support new alignment techniques (ORPO, SimPO)
Extensive documentation and examples from HuggingFace team
tools.best_for: Practitioners implementing custom RLHF, DPO, or preference alignment pipelines who need a scriptable, well-maintained library that integrates with the full HuggingFace ecosystem

tools.name: Replicate Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Per-second GPU billing during training; fine-tuned model hosting billed by inference requests; pricing competitive with Modal; check replicate.com/pricing
features: Simple API and web UI for triggering fine-tuning jobs
Particularly strong for image model fine-tuning (Flux, SDXL, LoRA)
One-click deployment of fine-tuned models to a hosted endpoint
No infrastructure setup — fully managed cloud execution
Large community of shared models and fine-tuning recipes
Supports Dreambooth and LoRA for image/multimodal models
tools.best_for: Developers and creators fine-tuning image generation models (Flux, SDXL) or needing fast, API-driven LLM fine-tuning without any DevOps setup
